description: Publish a folder of built static files from the agent's workspace to a Netlify site: first as a draft with a URL of its own, then live once published.
limitations: Static files only, built beforehand: Netlify runs no build and no Netlify Functions for them. Deploys only to the sites the login's settings pick. Netlify allows 3 deploys a minute and 100 a day.
setup_hint: Create a personal access token under Netlify → User settings → Applications, then pick the sites agents may deploy to. The token reaches every site of the account, so a team of its own for agents is safest.

sites.title: Sites
sites.description: The Netlify sites agents using this login may deploy to.

tools.name: sites
tools.description: The Netlify sites this login may deploy to, each with its live URL and the deploy it serves.

tools.name: deploy
tools.description: Upload a folder of built static files from the workspace to a site as a draft. The draft gets a URL of its own and the live site does not change. Build first: the folder is served exactly as it is, with index.html at its root, and _redirects and _headers files are honoured.

site.description: The site's name or id, one of those the sites tool lists.

folder_path.description: The folder to publish, under the agent's home, such as dist or /home/<agent>/app/dist.

title.description: A short note on what this deploy holds, shown in Netlify.

tools.name: deploy_status
tools.description: The state of one deploy: ready, still processing, or failed with Netlify's reason, with its draft URL.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Make a ready deploy the one the site serves at its live URL: a draft goes live, or an earlier deploy comes back.

prompt.guidance: Netlify publishes static files only. Build the site in the workspace first, then deploy the output folder as a draft and check its draft URL. Publish it to the live URL only when the task asks for the site to go live.
